methods.title: Methods with Parameters and Return Values
whereToLook: Check that getLength, getWidth, and getArea are each written as their own method with the return type and parameters described in the README.
Make sure each method uses a return statement to send the value back, instead of printing it directly inside the method.
Call each method from main() and store the value it returns in a variable.

scanner.title: Reading Input with Scanner
whereToLook: Make sure you create a Scanner object using System.in before you try to read any input.
Check that your prompt text matches the wording in the README before you call nextDouble().
Pass the same Scanner object into getLength and getWidth instead of creating a new one inside each method.

output.title: Displaying the Results
whereToLook: Make sure you are calling displayData with the length, width, and area variables rather than typing numbers into the message.
Check that getArea is being used to calculate the area instead of typing a calculated number directly.

closing.title: Closing the Program
whereToLook: Check that System.exit(0) is called after the landing zone's data has been displayed.

sourceChecks.name: Uses Scanner
sourceChecks.message: This challenge requires you to use a Scanner to read the user's input.

sourceChecks.name: Defines a getLength method
sourceChecks.message: You need a method named getLength that asks the user for the length and returns it.

sourceChecks.name: Defines a getWidth method
sourceChecks.message: You need a method named getWidth that asks the user for the width and returns it.

sourceChecks.name: Defines a getArea method
sourceChecks.message: You need a method named getArea that accepts length and width and returns the area.

sourceChecks.name: Defines a displayData method
sourceChecks.message: You need a method named displayData that displays the length, width, and area.

sourceChecks.name: Closes the program with System.exit
sourceChecks.message: Your program should close itself using System.exit() after displaying the results.

tests.name: Displays both prompts
tests.expectedOutput: Enter the landing zone's length in feet: Enter the landing zone's width in feet:
tests.message: Your program should display the exact prompts from the README before reading the length and the width.

possibleErrors.message: Your program produced no output. Make sure you print a prompt before reading input with the Scanner.
Check that your length prompt reads exactly "Enter the landing zone's length in feet:" and your width prompt reads exactly "Enter the landing zone's width in feet:".

tests.name: Calculates and displays area for length 5, width 3
tests.message: With a length of 5 and a width of 3, your program should display a length of 5.0, a width of 3.0, and an area of 15.0.

possibleErrors.message: Check that getArea multiplies the length and width parameters, and that displayData is called with the length, width, and area variables.

tests.name: Calculates and displays area for length 42, width 13
tests.message: With a length of 42 and a width of 13, your program should display a length of 42.0, a width of 13.0, and an area of 546.0.

possibleErrors.message: Your output still contains 15.0, which was the area from the previous test's numbers (5 x 3), even though different length and width values were provided this time. Make sure getArea is using the parameters passed into it rather than fixed numbers.
Check that getLength and getWidth are returning the values entered by the user for this run, not values left over from before.

tests.name: Calculates and displays area for length 1850, width 3650
tests.message: With a length of 1850 and a width of 3650, your program should display a length of 1850.0, a width of 3650.0, and an area of 6752500.0.

possibleErrors.message: Your output still contains 546.0, which was the area from the previous test's numbers (42 x 13), even though different length and width values were provided this time. Make sure your program is using the values entered by the user rather than a fixed result.
Your program may be waiting for more input than it needs. Make sure you only call nextDouble() once for length and once for width.
